# The rulings

<!-- GENERATED by tools/render_rulings.py. Do not edit; edit the TOML. -->

Composition spec **1.0.0**, 26 rulings.

A ruling is one decision the composer makes, written down and given an id that never changes meaning. A number published under a ruling id means the same thing forever, which is why rulings are superseded by new ids rather than edited.

Check what your installation carries with `nonius spec list`.

## Core

### `CORE-ALL-0001` — Scalar type tags, with bool tested before int

A scalar's type tag is one of bool, int, float, str, null. `bool` is tested before `int`
because bool is a subclass of int in Python; a boolean answer that reported itself as an
integer would become type-compatible with numeric slots and produce links that type-check
but mean nothing.

Calibration cases: `manifest-roundtrip-001`

### `CORE-ALL-0002` — Canonical serialization: sorted keys, 12 significant digits, no timestamps

Every artifact is serialized with sorted keys, floats quantized to 12 significant digits,
and no timestamp or hash-order dependence anywhere. Byte-identity is claimed per platform
and tested under two PYTHONHASHSEED values; cross-OS byte-identity is not claimed.

### `CORE-ALL-0003` — An item declares slots, results and nothing the composer interprets

An item is an id, a set of typed named input slots, a set of typed named results, an
optional stratum label, and an opaque adapter payload the core never inspects. Slot and
result names must be unique within an item. An item with no results cannot be an upstream
component; an item with no slots cannot be a downstream component; both are legal and are
reported by the audit rather than rejected.

Calibration cases: `manifest-roundtrip-001`

### `CORE-ALL-0004` — float and null are not composable in v1

Only bool, int and str may carry a link. float is excluded because exact equality on
floats is not a defensible link relation, and a declared tolerance would make the
composite's gold approximate, which defeats the by-construction claim the instrument
rests on. null is excluded because a null result carries no information to propagate.
Both are declared limitations with a stated reason, not oversights.

Calibration cases: `link-float-refused-001`

## Depth

### `DEPTH-ALL-0001` — Depth is the number of components; links number depth minus one — **superseded**

A composite's depth is its component count. A depth-1 composite is a single item and is
identical to the singleton it came from, which is what makes the bridge table exact at
depth 1. A depth-d composite carries d-1 links along any path, but the shape is a DAG,
not necessarily a path: a fan-in composite with one sink and d-1 upstream components has
depth d and d-1 links.

**Why.**

The convention has to be pinned before anything is measured because the two readings
differ by one item and the difference is visible in published arithmetic. A source record
for this work predicted that a system at 0.8385 single-item accuracy 'lands near 0.35 at
d=5'. 0.8385^5 = 0.4145 and 0.8385^6 = 0.3476, so the 0.35 figure was computed from six
components -- i.e. that record was counting links, not components, and calling the count
d. Under this ruling that prediction is a depth-6 prediction.

Calibration cases: `chain-depth3-path-001`

Superseded by `DEPTH-ALL-0003`.

### `DEPTH-ALL-0002` — Fan-in raises depth without lengthening the longest path

Component count, not longest path, is the quantity the independence product bound is
taken over: a composite is failed if any component is failed, regardless of the shape
that joins them. So a sink with k free slots fed by k distinct upstream components is a
depth-(k+1) composite. On a corpus whose link graph is shallow this is the only way to
reach higher depths without authoring items, and it is reported separately from path
depth so the two are never conflated.

Calibration cases: `chain-fanin-depth3-001`

### `DEPTH-ALL-0003` — Depth is the number of components, and does not determine the link count

A composite's depth is its component count. A depth-1 composite is a single item and is
identical to the singleton it came from, which is what makes the bridge table exact at
depth 1.

Depth does not determine how many links a composite has, in either direction. A simple
path of d components carries d-1 links; a fan-in of d components also carries d-1, but
only one along any path; and fan-out -- one component feeding several slots -- lets a
chain carry more than d-1. Component count is the quantity the independence product bound
is taken over, which is why it is the one called depth. Longest path is reported beside it
and never as it.

**Why.**

Supersedes DEPTH-ALL-0001, whose title and statement both asserted that links number
depth minus one. That is true only of a simple path. Counter-example on the shipped
calibration corpus: a chain over sum-a and dual-a with links sum-a.total -> subject_a and
sum-a.total -> subject_b has depth 2 and two links. LINK-ALL-0004 bounds incoming links
per slot, not per component, so nothing forbids it.

The convention still has to be pinned before anything is measured, because the two
readings of "depth" differ by one item and the difference is visible in published
arithmetic. A source record for this work predicted that a system at 0.8385 single-item
accuracy 'lands near 0.35 at d=5'. 0.8385^5 = 0.4145 and 0.8385^6 = 0.3476, so the 0.35
figure was computed from six components -- that record was counting links and calling the
count d. Under this ruling that prediction is a depth-6 prediction.

Calibration cases: `chain-depth3-path-001`

## Links

### `LINK-ALL-0001` — Type compatibility is necessary for a link

A link from an upstream result to a downstream slot requires the result's type tag to
equal the slot's type tag, and that tag to be composable (CORE-ALL-0004). This is a
necessary condition and not a sufficient one.

Calibration cases: `link-live-threshold-001`, `link-type-mismatch-001`

### `LINK-ALL-0002` — A link is admissible only if it is live over the upstream codomain

A link is admissible iff the downstream item's result set takes more than one distinct
value as the substituted slot ranges over the upstream result variable's codomain. A link
that fails this test is dead: the downstream answer does not depend on the upstream
answer, so a system can skip the upstream component entirely and still be scored correct.
Liveness is measured by running the oracle, never inferred from a declaration.

**Why.**

This is the ruling with evidence behind it, and it is why type compatibility alone is not
enough. Measured on a committed four-model archive of 100 programs: 3190 of 9900 ordered
item pairs (32.2%) are type-compatible, which clears the 20% threshold that a source
record set for feasibility -- but only 690 of 9900 (7.0%) carry a link that is live under
this ruling. A composer checking types alone would emit a corpus that is roughly
four-fifths degenerate. Those degenerate composites do not fail silently: they exceed
their own independence product bound and are quarantined (BOUND-ALL-0003), so a
type-only composer manufactures quarantine faster than it manufactures difficulty.

Calibration cases: `link-dead-lookup-miss-001`, `link-live-threshold-001`

### `LINK-ALL-0003` — An unbounded codomain is probed with a declared, versioned set

When an upstream result declares no codomain, liveness is tested against the declared
probe set rather than against an arbitrary sample, so that a liveness verdict is
reproducible and reviewable. The probe set is part of the spec and changing it is a
spec-major change, because it can move a link from dead to live and therefore change
which composites exist.

The v1 probe set for int is: 0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 50, 100, 1000, 10000, 60000, -1.

**Why.**

Chosen to straddle the decision boundaries a comparison-based consumer is likely to
carry -- zero, small counts, round magnitudes, and one negative -- without being tuned to
any particular corpus. It is deliberately small: a large probe set makes almost every
slot look live by finding some exotic value that moves it, which would defeat the purpose.

Calibration cases: `link-live-threshold-001`, `link-unbounded-probe-001`

### `LINK-ALL-0004` — A slot takes at most one incoming link

Each downstream slot is fed by at most one upstream result. A component may be upstream
of many links (fan-out) and a component may have many of its slots fed (fan-in), but a
single slot with two sources is not a substitution and is refused.

### `LINK-ALL-0005` — Chains are acyclic and stored in topological order

The link graph of a chain must be acyclic, and a chain stores its components in
topological order so that evaluating them in stored order is always legal. Ties break on
the order the components were supplied, never on set iteration, so the ordering is
deterministic.

### `LINK-ALL-0006` — Component reuse is counted and reported, and bounded by a declared ceiling

A component appearing in many composites makes the per-item accuracies used by the
product bound non-exchangeable, so the bound over-counts. nonius records the reuse
multiplicity of every component in an emitted set and refuses to report a product bound
when the maximum multiplicity exceeds the declared ceiling. The ceiling is a parameter
with no default: a caller must state it, because the tolerable amount depends on how the
bound will be read.

## Emission

### `EMIT-ALL-0001` — Literal suppression: a substituted slot must not survive in the presentation

A realized composite must not contain, anywhere in its presentation, a literal binding
for a slot that a link feeds. The link is symbolic: the downstream refers to the upstream
result, it does not quote its value. A realization that leaves the value visible is
refused at emit time with LiteralLeakError.

**Why.**

This is the shortcut the obvious reading of 'substitute the answer into the input
literals of the next item' produces, and it is fatal rather than cosmetic. If the
downstream's source prints the upstream's answer, a system reads it instead of computing
it, the composite is no harder than its last component, and it beats its own product
bound -- so the instrument's own validity gate would quarantine the entire emitted set.
Refusing at emit time turns a silent corpus-wide invalidity into one loud error.

Calibration cases: `chain-suppression-001`

### `EMIT-ALL-0002` — Gold agreement: two independent computations must agree

A composite's gold is accepted only if the realization's gold equals the gold obtained by
evaluating the components one at a time in topological order, substituting each link's
upstream value into the downstream binding before evaluating it. Disagreement raises
GoldDisagreementError and the composite is not emitted.

**Why.**

The instrument's entire claim is that a composite's gold is an exact deterministic
function of the component golds. That claim is checkable rather than assertable: the
chained-component evaluation and the realized composite's own evaluation are two
independent routes to the same number, and they must agree. This is the check that would
catch a realizer that quietly changed the semantics while merging.

Calibration cases: `chain-depth3-path-001`

### `EMIT-ALL-0003` — Composite identity is a content hash over shape, links and spec version

A composite's id is a truncated sha256 over its component ids in topological order, its
links, and the rulings version that produced it. Result names in the gold are qualified
by component position, not by item id, so the same item used twice in one composite stays
distinguishable and the gold's key set is a function of the chain's shape. The hash
changes if and only if the composite's meaning changes.

Calibration cases: `chain-depth3-path-001`

### `EMIT-ALL-0004` — Emission issues no model calls

Composing, checking and auditing are offline and free. No stage of nonius contacts a
model, a network service or a paid endpoint; running the emitted composites against
systems is the practitioner's own harness call, outside this tool.

## The bound

### `BOUND-ALL-0001` — The independence product bound is a prediction, not the oracle

For a system with recorded per-component accuracies p_i on the exact components of a
composite, the independence prediction for that composite is the product of the p_i. This
is the null the measurement is read against. It is never used to decide whether an answer
is correct: correctness is decided by the composed gold alone.

Calibration cases: `bound-product-001`

### `BOUND-ALL-0002` — The noise band comes from the archive's own replicates

The band within which a measured composite accuracy counts as agreeing with its product
prediction is derived from the replicate variation already present in the supplied
archive at its own k, by a seeded percentile bootstrap over the per-draw verdicts. It is
not a chosen constant. An archive with k = 1 supports no band, and nonius refuses to
quarantine rather than inventing one.

### `BOUND-ALL-0003` — Quarantine is exclusion, not failure

A composite whose measured accuracy exceeds its independence product prediction by more
than the noise band is quarantined as shortcut-contaminated: it is excluded from scoring
and reported, never counted as a system success. Quarantine is a verdict about the item,
not about the system.

Calibration cases: `bound-product-001`

### `BOUND-ALL-0004` — The quarantine rate is reported against a pre-registered ceiling

The fraction of composites quarantined at each depth is reported alongside the ceiling
declared before measurement. Without a declared ceiling the gate can only ever confirm
itself: composites that beat the bound are discarded as invalid and composites that match
it are reported as confirmation, which is a rule that cannot fail. nonius therefore
requires the ceiling as an explicit parameter and prints it next to the observed rate.

**Why.**

Recorded in this cell's own risk register: 'that is a rule which can only ever confirm
itself unless the quarantine rate is pre-registered with a ceiling ... Without that
ceiling the gate is a confirmation wearing a kill test's clothes.'

## The audit

### `AUDIT-ALL-0001` — The composability verdict taxonomy — **superseded**

An audit returns exactly one verdict:
  not_composable        -- no live link exists anywhere in the item set;
  composable_to_depth_k -- live links exist and the largest constructible component
                           count is k, with k stated;
  composable            -- live links exist and component count is bounded only by the
                           requested target rather than by the link graph.
The verdict is always accompanied by the reasons: which items cannot start a chain, which
cannot continue one, and which type tags carry no live link.

Calibration cases: `audit-verdict-001`

Superseded by `AUDIT-ALL-0005`.

### `AUDIT-ALL-0002` — Predictions are computed on the constructible population

Any predicted accuracy, dead fraction, floored fraction, discriminating fraction or
between-system gap the audit reports is computed by sampling composites the link graph
can actually build, not by sampling components uniformly from the item set. A uniform
prediction describes a population the composer cannot emit.

**Why.**

Measured on a committed four-model archive of 100 programs, with the same archive and the
same unit in both arms -- only the population differs:

  depth  population       n     discriminating    top-two gap   floored
    2    constructible   729        0.5446          0.2379       0.4554
    2    uniform        5000        0.7710          0.1121       0.2012
    3    constructible   134        0.7164          0.0294       0.2836
    3    uniform        5000        0.7172          0.1362       0.2794
    5    constructible   732        0.3279          0.0120       0.6721
    5    uniform        5000        0.5478          0.1398       0.4522

The uniform figure is not a conservative approximation of the constructible one; it
describes items the composer cannot emit. Note depth 3, where the two agree almost exactly
on the discriminating fraction (0.7164 against 0.7172) while differing 4.6-fold on the
between-system gap (0.0294 against 0.1362). A uniform prediction can therefore look
correct on one axis while being badly wrong on the axis a practitioner is buying.

The skew has a cause worth stating: on that asset only two of seven item families can
start a chain at all, and both are families the systems are worst at -- so every
constructible composite contains an already-hard component.

Calibration cases: `audit-constructible-001`

### `AUDIT-ALL-0003` — An audit issues no model calls and emits no composites

The audit is a pre-flight: it reads items, runs the practitioner's oracle to test
liveness, and reads an archive when one is supplied. It contacts nothing, spends nothing,
and produces no composite items. Its purpose is to answer 'can this benchmark be composed
at all, and how far' before any composites or completions are paid for.

### `AUDIT-ALL-0004` — Bounded coverage is stated, never silently applied

Where an audit bounds its own work -- a sampling cap, a path-enumeration limit, a
truncated probe set -- the bound and what it excluded are reported in the output. A
silently truncated search reads as 'covered everything' when it did not.

Calibration cases: `audit-verdict-001`

### `AUDIT-ALL-0005` — The composability verdict taxonomy, over the shapes the audit enumerates

An audit returns exactly one verdict:
  not_composable        -- no live link exists anywhere in the item set;
  composable_to_depth_k -- live links exist and k is the largest component count the audit
                           reached, with k stated;
  composable            -- live links exist and the upward search reached its own declared
                           limit without running out of chains, so no finite bound was
                           established.

k is a floor, not a maximum. The audit enumerates two shapes -- simple paths and
single-sink fan-ins -- and those are declared in every report's `caps` as
`enumerated_shapes`. A composite may legally be any acyclic shape, and a mixed one (a
fan-in whose sink then feeds a further component) can exceed k. The verdict is always
accompanied by the reasons: which items cannot start a chain, which cannot continue one,
and which type tags carry no live link.

**Why.**

Supersedes AUDIT-ALL-0001, which called k "the largest constructible component count".
It is not. Counter-example on the shipped calibration corpus, where the audit reports
composable_to_depth_3: the DAG {sum-a, sum-b} -> dual-a -> lk-live has four components and
three links, every link live, and it realizes cleanly through make_chain. The audit does
not find it because it is neither a path nor a single-sink fan-in.

Declaring the search space is the honest repair rather than widening it. Enumerating
general DAGs would change which composites the predicted rows are computed over, and so
would silently move every published prediction; a floor with its shapes stated is a
smaller claim that is actually true.

The `composable` branch was also wrong as written -- it said component count was "bounded
only by the requested target rather than by the link graph", while the code emits it when
the upward search hits MAX_DEPTH_SEARCH. A link graph really can bound construction above
that limit, so the old wording asserted the opposite of what the branch means.

Calibration cases: `audit-verdict-001`
